info.name: Luxy Galleria ERP API
info.description:
Machine-to-machine ERP API for luxygalleria.com, generated from `luxy-backend` source (`src/routes/erpRoutes.ts`, `src/controllers/erpController.ts`, `src/middlewares/erpAuth.ts`). Full specification: `docs/ERP-INTEGRATION-API-SPEC.md` (version 2.1).

**Setup**
1. Import this collection and the *Luxy Galleria ERP - Production* environment; select the environment (top right).
2. Set `erpKeyId` and `erpSecret` (Current value only; do not sync or share the secret). They are issued by Luxy Galleria through a secure channel.
3. Set `itemSku`, `categoryName`, `orderId` as needed. Your computer clock must be within 5 minutes of real time.

**Authentication** — every request is HMAC-signed by the collection pre-request script; no manual headers are needed:
- `X-ERP-Key-Id`: your key id
- `X-ERP-Timestamp`: Unix seconds
- `X-ERP-Signature`: hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, `timestamp.METHOD.pathWithQuery.sha256hex(body)`)

`pathWithQuery` is e.g. `/api/v1/erp/orders?page=1&limit=10`. The body is the exact raw JSON sent, empty for GET, or the image file bytes for Image Upload (see that request).

| HTTP | message | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `Invalid ERP credentials` | `X-ERP-Key-Id` missing or not configured on the server |
| 401 | `X-ERP-Timestamp missing or more than 300s from server time` | Computer clock wrong or request re-sent much later |
| 401 | `Invalid X-ERP-Signature` | Wrong secret, or body/path changed after signing |
| 401 | `Replayed request: …` | Same signature sent twice (re-send generates a new one automatically) |
| 503 | `ERP integration is not configured` | Server has no ERP keys |
| 429 | `Too many ERP requests…` | More than 600 requests/minute |

Responses: `{ "success": true, "message": "…", "data": … }` or `{ "success": false, "message": "…", "errors": [{ "code": "…", "field": "…" }] }`.

exec: // Luxy Galleria ERP request signing. Mirrors luxy-backend/src/middlewares/erpAuth.ts:
//   X-ERP-Signature = hex HMAC-SHA256(erpSecret, timestamp + "." + METHOD + "." + pathWithQuery + "." + hex SHA-256(body))
// body = the exact raw JSON text sent, "" for GET, or the image FILE bytes for POST /erp/images (via imageSha256).
throw new Error('Select the Luxy Galleria ERP environment and set erpKeyId and erpSecret (secret is 32+ characters).');
throw new Error('baseUrl must look like https://api.luxygalleria.com/api/v1 (no trailing slash).');
// Values used inside request bodies are fixed here, before hashing, so the signed and sent bytes match.
// Never use Postman dynamic variables such as {{$guid}} or {{$timestamp}} in a body: they resolve twice.
// Postman scripts cannot read the selected file, so its SHA-256 is supplied in the environment.
throw new Error('Set imageSha256 to the SHA-256 of the selected image (macOS/Linux: shasum -a 256 <file>; Windows: certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256).');
const signature = cryptoJs.HmacSHA256(timestamp + '.' + method + '.' + pathWithQuery + '.' + bodyHash, secret).toString(cryptoJs.enc.Hex);
// If the pre-request script fails, Postman still sends the request, unsigned, and the server answers 401 Invalid ERP credentials.
pm.test('request was signed by the collection pre-request script', function () {
pm.expect(pm.request.headers.has('X-ERP-Signature'), 'No X-ERP-Signature header: check the Postman Console for a pre-request script error').to.be.true;
// Every ERP response, success or error, uses the same envelope.
pm.test('response is the standard JSON envelope', function () {
try { msg = pm.response.json().message; } catch (e) { msg = pm.response.text().slice(0, 200); }

request.description:
**POST {{baseUrl}}/erp/items** — create a product with its variants, or update the product that already carries these SKUs.

- `201` + `action: "created"` when no SKU exists yet; `200` + `action: "updated"` when the SKUs belong to one existing product.
- On create, `name`, `description` and `category` are required. `category` must be the name (case-insensitive) or id of an **existing** website category.
- Each new variant needs `sku`, `offerPrice` and `actualPrice` (`offerPrice` ≤ `actualPrice`). `stock` is used **only when the variant is created**; change stock later with Stock Update.
- Unknown fields are rejected (`400`). Optional: `brand`, `brandId`, `imageUrls` (https, replaces the list), `variants[].volume|flavor|weight|image`.
- Errors: `400` validation / unknown category; `409 CONFLICT` SKUs on two products; `409 DUPLICATE_SKU`; `409 UNMAPPED_PRODUCT` when a website product with the same name has variants without a SKU (ask Luxy Galleria to set your SKU on it; nothing is created).

⚠️ **Production:** the website has no inactive-product flag, so a created item is visible on the storefront. Use an approved test SKU.

exec: pm.test('data matches the documented schema', function () {

request.description:
**PATCH {{baseUrl}}/erp/items/{sku}** — change only the supplied fields of this SKU's variant and its product.

- Product fields: `name`, `description`, `category`, `brand`, `brandId`, `imageUrls`. Variant fields: `size`/`volume`, `flavor`, `offerPrice`, `actualPrice`, `weight`, `image`.
- At least one field. `stock` and `sku` are **not allowed** (`400`). Omitted fields, other variants and stock are untouched.
- Errors: `400` validation / price above MRP; `404` SKU not found; `409 DUPLICATE_SKU`.

exec: pm.test('data matches the documented schema', function () {

request.description:
**PUT {{baseUrl}}/erp/stock/{sku}** — set the **absolute** sellable quantity of one variant (not an adjustment).

- `quantity`: integer 0–1,000,000. `asOf`: ISO 8601 time the ERP figure was taken (here: the send time, set by the collection script).
- Website orders placed after `asOf` and units held by open website checkouts are subtracted: stored = max(0, quantity − pendingOrderQuantity − reservedQuantity). All are returned. Provisional until the ERP team confirms physical vs sellable stock.
- Same `asOf` again → `200`, `applied: false`. Older `asOf` than the last applied → `409 STALE_UPDATE`.
- Errors: `400` validation / `asOf` > 5 min in the future; `404` unknown SKU (never creates a product); `409 DUPLICATE_SKU`; `409 CONFLICT` when stock kept changing during the update (nothing written; retry as is).

query.description: ISO 8601; returns orders with updatedAt >= this

request.description:
**GET {{baseUrl}}/erp/orders** — orders page by page, oldest change first (sorted by `updatedAt`, then `orderId`).

- Query: `page` (≥1), `limit` (1–100, default 50), optional `status`, `paymentStatus`, `updatedSince`. Unknown parameters → `400`.
- Response also carries `pagination: { page, limit, total, pages }` next to `data`.
- Incremental sync: keep the newest `updatedAt` received and pass it as `updatedSince`; de-duplicate by `orderId`.
- `items[].sku` / `items[].name` are the values at purchase for orders placed since API version 2.1; older orders show current product data.
- Read-only. Copy an `orderId` from here into the environment for Order Details.

exec: pm.test('data matches the documented schema', function () {

request.description:
**GET {{baseUrl}}/erp/orders/{orderId}** — one order by website order id (24 hex characters).

- Adds `customer.phone`, `shippingAddress`, `payment` and `statusUpdatedAt` to the list fields.
- `shippingAddress` is `null` for store-pickup orders. GST is returned in `charges.tax` and per item (`taxRate`, `taxAmount`) when enabled.
- Not held by the website (so not returned): HSN codes, billing address, recipient name/phone, order number.
- Errors: `400` malformed id; `404` not found. Read-only.

exec: pm.test('data matches the documented schema', function () {

formdata.description: Select one JPG, PNG or WEBP file (max 15 MB)

request.description:
**POST {{baseUrl}}/erp/images** — upload one product image; returns a hosted `https` URL to use in `imageUrls` or `variants[].image`.

**How to send it from Postman**
1. Body → form-data → key `image` (type *File*) → **Select Files** → choose the image. No other form fields.
2. Compute the file's SHA-256 and paste it into the environment variable `imageSha256`:
   - macOS / Linux: `shasum -a 256 /path/to/image.png`
   - Windows: `certutil -hashfile C:\path\to\image.png SHA256`
3. Send. The signature covers the **file bytes**, not the multipart envelope; Postman scripts cannot read the selected file, which is why its hash is supplied. Update `imageSha256` whenever you pick a different file.

- JPG/JPEG, PNG or WEBP; extension, content type and actual bytes must agree. Max 15 MB.
- Errors: `400` no/extra file, wrong type; `401 Invalid X-ERP-Signature` if `imageSha256` is not the selected file's hash; `413` too large; `502` storage failed (retry); `503` storage not configured.
- ⚠️ Each successful call stores a new image in the website's Cloudinary account.

request.description:
**POST {{baseUrl}}/erp/webhooks/order-status** — the ERP tells the website an order's fulfilment status changed.

- `eventId` (unique per event; leave the environment value empty to auto-generate one per send), `orderId`, `status` (`processing` | `shipped` | `delivered` | `cancelled`), `occurredAt`. Optional `erpOrderId`, `trackingNumber`.
- Allowed: processing → shipped/delivered/cancelled; shipped → delivered/cancelled. `delivered` and `cancelled` are final.
- Outcomes (all `200`): `applied` (customer emailed once), `unchanged`, `stale` (older than last applied), or `duplicate: true` for a repeated `eventId`.
- Errors: `400` validation; `404` order not found; `409 INVALID_TRANSITION`; `409 CONFLICT` (erpOrderId mismatch or concurrent change — retry).

⚠️ **Production:** an applied change is visible to the customer and **emails them**. Use only an approved test order.

request.description:
**GET {{baseUrl}}/erp/items** — website products with all variants, newest change first.

- Query: `page` (≥1), `limit` (1–100, default 50), optional `search` (≤100 characters; case-insensitive match on product name or SKU). Unknown parameters → `400`.
- `pagination` is inside `data`.
- `variants[].sku` is `null` for variants that have no SKU yet; agree their item codes with Luxy Galleria using `variantId`.
- Read-only.

*Added in API version 2.1. Verified by a local Postman CLI run (see the spec, Section 15.7); not yet run against production.*
